title: Unordered Container Traversal Used Where Stable Output Is Required
pattern: Hash-map/set iteration determines the order of an output expected to be deterministic, or an external serialized payload relies on unspecified container order where consumers, signatures, caches, or reproducibility require stable bytes or ordering.
why_bad: Standard hash containers use randomized hashing to prevent hash-DoS attacks, so their iteration order is unspecified and may differ between executions. Equivalent logical data can then produce different sequential or byte representations, breaking reproducibility, order-sensitive consumers, content-based keys, test assertions, or signature verification that expects a canonical representation.
detection: Subcase A: trace `HashMap`/`HashSet` iteration into sequential strings, lists, keys, files, or build output and identify the deterministic-output contract. Subcase B: inspect direct text/binary serialization of unordered containers and determine whether downstream verification or consumers require a stable representation and whether the serializer already canonicalizes it. If order is semantically irrelevant and no byte-stability requirement exists, record no violation.
counterexample:
Internal unordered lookup, order-insensitive formats/consumers without canonical-byte requirements, self-ordering serializers, and explicit deterministic sorting are legitimate:
```rust
let key = map.get("id"); // internal lookup only

let mut keys: Vec<_> = map.keys().collect();
keys.sort(); // explicit deterministic order
```
source: *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* by Martin Kleppmann (Chapter 3); *Code Complete* by Steve McConnell (p. 211); *Software Engineering at Google* by Titus Winters et al. (Chapter 8, p. 305).
